correctness.rationale: The transform convention is unnormalized A_f(x,χ)=∑ f(t) overline(f(t−x)) overline(χ(t)), for finite abelian G, proper H of order h>=2, y outside, z nonzero. Expanding four disjoint product types proves h−1 nonzero H-shift rows of q=N/h characters and a zero-shift row with N entries minus q/r cancellations iff r is even and |z|²=h. For quotient order r>2 the ±(y+H) cross-cosets do not overlap, contributing 2hN. For r=2 they coincide, cross-row factors z+bar z overline χ(x); evaluation of character χ(x) over its o(x) roots produces exactly N/o(x) vanished entries iff d=ord(−bar z/z) divides o(x). This gives the complete support formulas, all phase-attainable levels, minimum at calibrated |z|²=h and d|gcd orders, and the lower bound from o(x)>=2 with sharp elementary two-torsion equality classification. Independent exact Fourier enumeration over cyclic Z8 with H even and z=2,2i returned support 41, with z=1 support 42; a binary two-dimensional equality check and original exact cyclotomic test cases corroborate. These finite examples are not an arbitrary-group proof.

value.rationale: A subgroup indicator is a natural exact localization extremizer in finite time-frequency analysis; adding one point outside the subgroup is the minimal structural perturbation. Classifying exact cancellations shows an otherwise invisible order-two quotient produces an arithmetic phase staircase, provides a sharp universal gap with exact equality configurations, and distinguishes all higher quotient orders. This useful structural instability result neither claims a general new uncertainty principle nor noise-stable estimates.

limitations: Exact-zero support, one added off-subgroup impulse in finite abelian groups; no noise threshold or general class of signals.
Unindexed alternative signal-processing terminology remains possible.
